To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Kiss2 decapeptides significantly modulate the hypothalamic expression of reproduction-related genes in the half-smouth tongue sole (C. semilaevis).
the Kiss2 decapeptides significantly increase the amounts of gnii and kiss2 m RNAs, but significantly decrease the amounts of gnihr and Kiss2R mRNAs in hypothalamus of the half-smooth tong sole.
Kiss2 decapeptides can directly regulate hypothalamic gene expression, and this regulation is tissue specific and differential.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular cloning, tissue expression and functional characterization of Kiss2 and its receptor in the half-smouth tongue sole (C. semilaevis) and the in vitro effects of the Kiss2 decapeptid on reproduction-related gene in the hypothalamo-pituitary-gonadal axis.
the role of Kiss1 and Kiss2 peptides in the regulation of reproduction-related genes in the hypothalamo-pituitary-gonadal axis of a teleost, the half-smooth tonge sole.
the characterization and functional analysis of kisspeptin (kiss2) receptor (kiss2r) and the effects of kiss2 on reproduction-related genes expression in half-smooth tongue soles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Kiss2 has a direct and positive regulatory effect on gnih and kiss expression in tongue sole, and a negative regulatory effect on gnihr and its receptor kiss2r expression.
the Kiss2/KissR system is involved in the regulation of GnIH expression and that the Kiss2 receptor may be a target for GnIH.
Kiss2 has a stimulatory effect on GnRH and GnIH neurons, and an inhibitory effect on GnRH receptor and kisspeptin receptor neurons in the teleost brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
kiss2r gene is highly expressed in the hypothalamo-pituitary-gonadal axis of the tongue sole, which is consistent with a role for Kiss2/KissR in the control of gonadal functions.
the kiss2r is expressed widely in the tongue sole, and the hypothalamic Kiss2 decapeptid can regulate the expression of some reproduction-related genes in the hypothalamuses of this teleost fish.

the Kiss2/Kiss1R system plays a critical role in regulating reproduction-related gene expression and that Kiss2 is a novel regulator of GnIH and Kiss1/2 systems in the hypothalamo-pituitary-gonadal axis of teleosts.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Kiss2 is involved in regulating the expression of reproduction-related genes at the level of the hypothalamus in tongue sole, which may provide a new insight into the reproductive control of this species.
the Kiss2/KissR2 system plays an essential role in the regulation of GnIH and GnIH receptor in the hypothalamopituitary axis of teleost fishes.

kisspeptin signaling may play an important role in the regulation of reproduction-related genes in the hypothalamo-pituitary axis of teleost fish, but the precise mechanism of action remains to be elucidated.
